A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PiCa work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original PiCa results on NLP and vision benchmarks, projection and weight-sharing ablations, and empirical singular-vector analyses. These qualify independently of baseline results attributed to prior work.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and additionally reports Full-FT reproductions, GPU-memory measurements, and comparisons with weight-sharing baselines.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same fixed, layer-specific column-space projections, gradient aggregation, shared compact parameters, and Adam updates. Renaming theta to B and explicitly writing W = W0 + U_r B in Section 3.3 clarify the existing procedure rather than introduce a different method.

E1.justification: Both versions retain MetaMathQA-40K with GSM-8K/MATH evaluation, the eight commonsense benchmarks, GLUE, VTAB-1K, and DreamBooth. The new learning-rate, memory, and sharing comparisons do not establish additional dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The existing benchmark comparator sets remain. New Table 13 adds weight-sharing adaptations of LoRA, DoRA, SVFT_R, and SVFT_B to the Gemma-2B mathematical-reasoning comparison. These are targeted additions within existing method families; the Full-FT reruns change settings rather than comparator identity.

E3.justification: Appendix C newly reports Full-FT reproductions for Gemma-7B and LLaMA-3-8B using lower learning rates, stated as 1e-6/5e-6. Sections C.4–C.5 introduce peak-GPU-memory measurement and comparisons under a common weight-sharing scheme. Existing PiCa hyperparameter tables, datasets, and task metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The existing projection-choice, sharing, rank, and subspace-alignment analyses remain. v3 adds targeted checks of whether PiCa's advantage persists when competing methods also share weights, actual memory costs beyond parameter counts, and Full-FT learning-rate sensitivity. These extend the diagnostic evidence without replacing the original analyses.

E5.justification: Table 10 retains the same plus/minus summaries for singular-vector alignment and perturbations. Neither version supplies task-performance seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests, and v3 introduces no new statistical reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces Gemma-7B Full-FT GSM-8K/MATH scores of 74.67/25.70 with 78.09/30.98, and LLaMA-3-8B scores of 64.13/16.24 with 76.57/26.12. These lower-learning-rate reproductions reverse Full-FT versus PiCa rankings in three of four cases, materially revising the reference comparisons. Tables 12–13 also add memory measurements and shared-baseline results. Existing PiCa and PEFT accuracy entries remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Lemma 3.1, Definition 1, Theorems 1–2, and the assumptions and proofs in Appendices A–B are mathematically unchanged. The explicit reparameterization restates Algorithm 1; the added discussion of optimality changes interpretation rather than the formal results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: theoretically motivated column-space projection, parameter savings through weight sharing, and competitive or superior NLP/vision performance under comparable parameter budgets. The additional experiments do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 newly states that the theorem does not establish globally optimal projection or guarantee task-optimal performance, and revises the motivation for small updates. Appendix C adds learning-rate sensitivity as an explanation for Full-FT differences and attributes SVFT's memory overhead to retaining full singular-vector matrices. The existing loading-versus-storage limitation remains.

D1.justification: v3 adds an official PiCa implementation link and an explicit zero-initialized reparameterization with matrix dimensions in Section 3.3. It also documents reproduction learning rates and shared-baseline configurations. The original implementation and hyperparameter information is retained; the new memory comparison leaves units and hardware unspecified.

R1.justification: v3 adds Meng et al.'s PiSSA to the SVD-related literature and explicitly contrasts conventional LoRA initialization with exploiting pretrained geometry. The broader positioning remains. The updated publication details for Cho et al. refer to the same previously cited work.

P1.justification: v3 revises the small-update motivation, expands theoretical and implementation explanations, standardizes terminology, and renames the shared parameter from theta to B. It also swaps the two retained Appendix C subsections, adds acknowledgments, and updates the publication header. The overall narrative structure remains.

P2.justification: v3 adds tables for Full-FT reproduction, memory usage, and shared-baseline comparisons. Existing tables and Figure 3 are redistributed, with corresponding appendix renumbering and caption edits. The original plots and established table formats are largely retained.

improvement.justification: The lower-learning-rate Full-FT reproductions and shared-baseline controls improve comparison credibility, while the explicit implementation equation, code link, and optimality qualification improve clarity. These are targeted gains to an otherwise retained paper. The new memory evidence is useful but limited by unspecified units and hardware, so the additions support a modest overall improvement.
